messages:
Carla (CS): heads-up — we need a short, low-friction customer note for ~12 EU onboarding tenants impacted by yesterday's maintenance-induced latency spike. target: send by EOD.
Ben P.: tl;dr from infra: dedicated shard failed during a rolling kernel upgrade, failover loop caused 10-40s tail latency for onboarding webhook and SSO calls for ~25 minutes. root cause being investigated but we have a mitigation path.
Carla (CS): ok can you write a 1-paragraph RCA + mitigation and a suggested credit? small targeted credit for onboarding time. keep it plain-language.
Ben P.: RCA draft: "During an automated kernel rollout in EU-west, a subset of dedicated serving shards experienced repeated failovers due to a rare device driver timing interaction. This produced elevated queueing and intermittent 5xx/timeout responses for customer onboarding flows for ~25 minutes. We rolled back the kernel, applied a per-shard circuit breaker, and validated normal traffic. Full driver patch queued for next maintenance window."
Alice N.: customer-facing message draft below. pls review tone — want to reassure, offer 1 week of onboarding credits (waive onboarding usage for next 7 days), and invite to office hours.
Alice N.: ```Hi <Account Team>,
We9re following up about a brief disruption on [date] that affected onboarding and SSO for some EU customers. Between 09:12-09:37 UTC our system experienced higher latency and intermittent timeouts while processing onboarding webhooks and SSO handshakes. Our engineers identified a kernel-level issue on a small group of dedicated serving shards and reverted the rollout to restore normal service. We9ve applied a temporary safety measure to prevent recurrence, and a permanent driver fix is planned and tested for the next maintenance window.
We9re sorry for the disruption. As a gesture we9ll apply a 7day onboarding credit to any affected tenant and we9re hosting a short office hours session tomorrow at 15:00 UTC to answer questions and help finish any stuck onboard flows.
If you9d like us to escalate for an account-specific follow-up or priority sync, reply to this message and we9ll route to an engineer.
Thanks,
Redwood Customer Success
```
David Ops: nit — change "09:12-09:37 UTC" to the exact window we observed: 2026-03-19 09:11:45-09:36:20 UTC. also suggest adding the monitored remediation steps we executed: rollback, per-shard circuit breaker, throttled rejoin.
Eve (AM): list of affected accounts I pulled from the incident tag: AcmeRetail, PaperTrail Inc, LumaAI (trial), BlueBox EU, Qoncept, Trident EDU, 6 SMB trials. Prioritize AcmeRetail and LumaAI for a direct AM reachout.
Carla (CS): great — update message with exact timestamps and remediation bullets. also capture a short FAQ line about billing impact and next steps.
Alice N.: updated draft: ```Hi <Account Team>,
On 2026-03-19 09:11:45-09:36:20 UTC we observed elevated latency and intermittent timeouts impacting onboarding webhooks and SSO for a small set of EU tenants. Engineers traced the issue to a kernel timing interaction on a subset of dedicated serving shards during a scheduled kernel rollout. To restore stability we rolled back the rollout, applied a per-shard circuit breaker and a throttled shard rejoin policy, and verified normal traffic. A permanent driver patch is scheduled and validated for the next maintenance window.
What we9re doing for you: 
• We will apply a 7-day onboarding credit to affected tenants (no action required).
• We9re hosting office hours on 2026-03-20 15:00 UTC to help finish stuck onboard flows — register here: https://redwood.example/office-hours
• If your onboarding was interrupted and you want a priority assist, reply and we9ll set up a 1:1 with an engineer.
Billing FAQ: This incident will not affect past billing. The 7-day onboarding credit will be applied to billing for affected tenants and shown on the next invoice.
We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience.
— Redwood Customer Success
```
InfraBot: incident tag created: INC-2026-0319-042; severity: P2; status: triaged -> in-progress -> mitigated.
Ben P.: one small suggestion: remove the words "kernel timing interaction" from the customer-facing note; replace with "a rare kernel upgrade interaction" — less technical.
Carla (CS): agreed, keep it accessible. also add a single-line feedback ask: "Was this communication helpful? reply with yes/no or quick note."
Eve (AM): i'll ping AcmeRetail and LumaAI directly after we send the broadcast and schedule the priority assist for both.
Alice N.: final draft attached below (ready to send): ```Hi <Account Team>,
On 2026-03-19 09:11:45-09:36:20 UTC we experienced a brief service disruption that increased latency and caused intermittent timeouts for onboarding webhooks and SSO for a small set of EU tenants. Engineers traced this to a rare interaction during an automated kernel upgrade on a limited set of dedicated serving shards. To restore service we reverted the upgrade, applied a per-shard safety breaker, and throttled shard rejoin — we confirmed normal traffic shortly after.
What we are doing for you:
• We will apply a 7-day onboarding credit to affected tenants (no action needed).
• Office hours: 2026-03-20 15:00 UTC — https://redwood.example/office-hours
• Priority assist: reply to this message to request a 1:1 engineer session.
Billing note: this incident will not change prior invoices. The onboarding credit will appear on your next billing statement.
We9re sorry for the disruption. Was this communication helpful? Reply with yes/no or a short note.
— Redwood Customer Success
```
Carla (CS): approved. Ben, David — confirm we9re good to send.
Ben P.: confirmed.
David Ops: confirmed, go ahead. I9ll post the brief technical attachable note for accounts that request deeper detail.
Carla (CS): sending now. tagging AMs to follow-up on priority accounts. :white_check_mark:
